chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The believers are on seven ranks: One of them is in an additional favor from God, the Exalted, which does not remove him from his rank to the rank of another; and among them are the witnesses of God among His creatures; and among them are the noble ones; and among them are the tested ones; and among them are the brave ones; and among them are the people of patience; and among them are the people of piety; and among them are the people of forgiveness.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven ranks of believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hierarchy in *Al-Khisal* to illustrate the stratified spiritual states of the faithful, emphasizing that divine favor (*ziyadah*) enhances one's rank without necessarily altering their fundamental station. The classification moves from the martyrs and nobles to those defined by trials, bravery, patience, piety, and ultimate forgiveness, reflecting a comprehensive view of spiritual development in Shia tradition. This framework underscores the dynamic nature of *iman* (faith) as a journey through various degrees of closeness to God.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-32 Al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

There are seven ranks for a believer. None of them would go beyond their rank. Those with a given rank may get honored by the Honorable the Exalted God and be promoted, but they would never achieve a different rank. One group are God’s witnesses for His creatures. One group are the noble ones. One group are the examined ones. One group are the brave ones. One group are the patient ones. One group are the pious ones and one group are those who seek forgiveness.”
